text: The highlight of our Jordan trip. Noor and her mother were so warm, and the maqluba lunch was the best meal we had all week. Watching the stone press was fascinating.
Beautiful olive grove and great stories about the family history. Hard to find the farm though - our taxi got lost twice and there is no sign on the main road.
We loved picking za'atar in the garden and the sage tea. I wish we could have bought more products, the shop only had a few jars left.
Lovely people but the tour felt long in the afternoon heat and there was not much shade between the grove and the press.
Un accueil chaleureux et un déjeuner délicieux. Le pressoir en pierre est impressionnant. Dommage que la réservation par WhatsApp soit un peu lente.
Wir durften beim Pressen helfen, das war ein Erlebnis! Das Olivenöl ist hervorragend, wir haben drei Flaschen gekauft.
Our guide translated for us but some of the stories got lost in translation. Still a very authentic experience and the oil was excellent.
My father uses a wheelchair and they took him through the grove on the farm cart. So kind and thoughtful. The toilet was clean too.
Good value for a full lunch and tour. We wanted to take a cooking class too but there was no option to book one.
تجربة رائعة، الضيافة كانت ممتازة والزيت طازج. نتمنى لو كان هناك ورشة لتعليم صنع الزعتر.
The kids loved feeding the chickens and running in the grove. Lunch was delicious. Parking was a bit difficult for our minivan.
Booked through a friend of a friend - it would be great if the farm had a proper listing online with photos and prices. We almost did not go because we could not find any information.
Came for the olive harvest in November last year and came back this spring with friends. Picking olives with the family is something we will never forget.
The tour was too long for us and the bus left before we could buy oil. Wish the shop opened earlier in the tour.
Fantastic za'atar - we have been using the jar we bought every morning since we got home. Please start selling online!
